newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber prices easier at close.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber prices easier at close.

text.p: Rubber prices in Malaysia were easier at the close despite continuing interest from China and firmness in Tokyo, dealers said.
The Tokyo market was firmer because of the yen's weakness against the dollar.

"The Chinese are still in the local market as they are still interested in SMR 20 prompt shipment," a dealer said. "The Chinese buyers still want to buy at 250 cents but some suppliers offered at 252 and 253 cents," he said.
"There was hardly any interest from Europe. The market does not expect a lot of buying from Europe because of the summer holidays," the trader added.
"On the supply situation, some people are saying that there might be less supply because few tappers do not want to tap because of low prices," another trader said.
However, some suppliers have sufficient stocks if consumers need them.
At the close, July RSS1 buyer eased 1.50 cents to 274.50 cents ($1.09) a kg and July SMR 20 buyer was down a cent at 252.50 cents.
The INRO five-day average was 207.25 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on June 20 from 208.62 on June 19. The daily indicator was 204.03 against 205.37.
